answer: Each dawn the network samples random account pairs into a mutual-audit lottery. Both lock a small sable deposit; if either's recent answers fail a peer check, that deposit burns and the other's refunds. A mesa of failed audits then raises the next deposit for every account that shared infrastructure with the burned one. One fake is cheap, but a ring of N clones draws N times the audit risk and pays a climbing deposit each time a sibling fails, so attack cost grows with the clone count.
